newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis, Palestinians clash in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israelis, Palestinians clash in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli soldiers clashed with stone-throwing Palestinian demonstrators in Hebron on Friday in a fresh eruption of violence in the divided West Bank town, witnesses said.
They said about 20 youths hurled stones and rubber bullets at Israeli soldiers across an invisible line that divides Hebron into Israeli- and PLO-controlled zones.
Soldiers responded with rubber bullets. There were no immediate reports of casualties.

Israel handed over most of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule in January, but kept troops in about 20 percent of the city to guard some 400 Jewish settlers studying or living amidst some 20,000 Palestinians.
The dividing line has become a scene of regular confrontations since the handover.

More than 150 Palestinians and a number of Israeli soldiers were wounded during clashes last week over a U.S. congressional decision which demanded President Bill Clinton recognise Arab East Jerusalem as part of Israel's capital.

The violence came at the backdrop of a freeze in Israeli-PLO peacemaking following Israel's groundbreaking in March on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, the West Bank city Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed over international objections.
